instruction: When I try to use 'll' command for detailed directory listings, I get "command not found". Could you set up this common alias for me so I can use 'll' as a shortcut for 'ls -alF'?

command: import pyautogui; import time; time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'alt', 't'); time.sleep(0.5)

metadata.explanation: Task requires adding the common 'll' alias to .bashrc. Evaluator checks if the alias line exists in .bashrc. Same pattern as original - adding shell configuration to fix a command not found error.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly uses vm_command_line to execute a shell command that checks for the alias in ~/.bashrc
Command logic is sound: 'grep -q' searches for the exact alias definition, outputs '1\n' on success, '0\n' on failure
Metric exact_match correctly receives rules dict and compares result with rules['expected']
Expected value '1\n' is semantically correct for the command's success output
Evaluator verifies the core requirement: adding 'alias ll=\'ls -alF\'' to .bashrc
Parameter handling is correct - metric receives rules dict directly (not wrapped in {'type': 'rule', 'rules': {...}})
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor consideration: The grep pattern uses single quotes in the alias definition. If user sets alias with double quotes (alias ll="ls -alF"), verification would fail. However, single quotes are the standard convention for this alias.
Minor consideration: Alias could theoretically be defined in other files like ~/.bash_aliases or ~/.profile, but ~/.bashrc is the standard location for user-defined aliases in Ubuntu.
